claims.text: The initial ball-milled MgAlTiVFeCo powder forms a simple BCC solid solution.
Spark plasma sintering at 1000 °C promotes rapid diffusion in MgAlTiVFeCo powder.
SPS at 1000 °C produces a dense microstructure.
SPS at 1000 °C precipitates uniformly distributed barrier oxides such as AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3.
The dense microstructure and uniformly distributed barrier oxides yield a continuous passive film.
The continuous passive film blocks chloride-ion penetration during corrosion testing.
Oxidation at 900 °C follows parabolic, diffusion-controlled kinetics.
Oxidation exhibits a biphasic growth pattern because protective oxide layers form.
Sintering at 1000 °C improves corrosion resistance relative to sintering at 850–950 °C.
Sintering at 1000 °C improves high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to sintering at 850–950 °C.
The alloy sintered at 1000 °C will attain approximately 96.7% relative density.
The alloy sintered at 1000 °C will attain approximately 1235 HV microhardness.
The 1000 °C sample will have a more positive corrosion potential than samples sintered at 850–950 °C.
The 1000 °C sample will have a lower corrosion current density than samples sintered at 850–950 °C.
Samples sintered at 850–950 °C have lower relative density than the 1000 °C sample.
Samples sintered at 850–950 °C have lower hardness than the 1000 °C sample.
The inferior corrosion and oxidation resistance of lower-temperature samples results from less effective barrier-phase formation.
The sintering temperature must remain below 1000 °C to prevent magnesium volatilization.
Sintering above 800 °C is required to ensure sufficient sintering and relative density greater than 80%.

contradictions.description: The intervention and central prediction specify sintering at exactly 1000 °C, whereas the boundary states that sintering must remain below 1000 °C to prevent magnesium volatilization.
